assertions.assertion: States IdentityServer has no built-in HSM/KMS provider and a custom ISigningKeyStore does not give non-exportable keys
assertions.rationale: Never states no built-in KMS provider; its approach is a custom ISigningCredentialStore, the opposite of the claim.

assertions.assertion: Subclasses DefaultTokenCreationService and overrides CreateJwtAsync to call the KMS async sign API, registering it as ITokenCreationService
assertions.rationale: No DefaultTokenCreationService subclass or ITokenCreationService; uses ISigningCredentialStore/IValidationKeysStore.

assertions.assertion: Registers the KMS public key as the signing credential with AddSigningCredential and disables automatic key management (KeyManagement.Enabled = false)
assertions.rationale: Disables key management but doesn't use AddSigningCredential with the public key; uses custom stores.

assertions.assertion: Takes alg and kid from the registered signing credential so the header matches discovery/JWKS
assertions.rationale: Doesn't take alg/kid from the registered credential in a token creation override.

assertions.assertion: Notes SAML signing does not go through ITokenCreationService and requires a private key, so this approach doesn't cover SAML
assertions.rationale: Says SAML needs an X.509 cert but not that it bypasses ITokenCreationService; admits uncertainty.

assertions.assertion: Mentions rotation is the developer's responsibility (publish new key via AddValidationKey ahead of time) and each token costs a KMS call
assertions.rationale: Doesn't mention developer-managed rotation via AddValidationKey or per-token KMS call cost.
